_meta.description: Everything Scripture Alone does: offline Bibles in nine languages, study mode with commentary and the original languages, camera notes, verse images, a Keepsake Bible and Apple Watch.
a-native-app-for.534255: A native app for Android phones and tablets, with its own Wear OS app, on Google Play.
a-toggle-away-tap.8c147a: A toggle away: tap a verse and the Study panel follows, with ranked cross-references (one tap there and back) and classic commentary from John Calvin, John Gill and Jamieson‑Fausset‑Brown. The commentary downloads the first time you open it; cross-references are there from the start.
add-the-translations-you.33c4e1: Add the translations you want, compare any two, and keep what you import to yourself.
an-illustrated-guide-to.7645a6: An illustrated guide to every feature, in your language — with step-by-step setup of your own ESV, CSB and NKJV keys, and of importing a study Bible or a Bible PDF. It's in the app under Aa › User Guide, or download the PDF.
anxious-grieving-lonely-tempted.da559a: Anxious, grieving, lonely, tempted, waiting? Topics gathers 72 things people go through, each with the passages that speak to it, in the translation you read. Type a word like “worried” into search and its topic comes first. English readers also get all of Nave's Topical Bible, A to Z.
auto-scroll-keeps-the.e753e5: Auto-scroll keeps the text moving at your pace and carries on into the next chapter — an accessibility feature for anyone who finds scrolling by hand difficult, or simply wants to read without touching the screen.
being-built-now-and.f37881: Being built now, and not in the app yet. They'll ship when they're ready.
browse-the-openly-licensed.b69d50: Browse the openly licensed translations eBible.org publishes, in your own language first, and download only the ones you choose — or open a USFM file or a DRM-free ePub you already own. The ESV, CSB and NKJV can't be given away by anyone, so they're read with your own free key from the publisher. Licenses to carry the ESV and CSB offline are still being sought.
cross-references-commentary-the.0d6a03: Cross-references, commentary, the original languages and the world of each chapter, a tap away.
design-a-verse-image.0a20c5: Design a verse image on your device from eight templates, or send a link that rebuilds the card in any browser from the link itself — nothing is stored on a server.
each-chapter-s-era.4b0bd3: Each chapter's era on a timeline of the biblical periods, an offline map of the places it names, and charts of the kings of Israel and Judah, Paul's journeys, the twelve tribes and the feasts of Israel.
english-american-standard-version.f99ec6: English — American Standard Version · Berean Standard Bible · King James Version
every-line-of-code.0797fb: Every line of code is public under the AGPL-3.0 license. Read it, check it, or build it yourself.
every-word-on-your.f912e8: Every word on your device, set the way it was printed, and as easy on the eyes as you want it.
free-with-no-ads.48eb07: Free, with no ads and no accounts. Every feature below is in the app today, except the last section.
hear-any-chapter-read.f4ef56: Hear any chapter read aloud with your device's voices, Premium and Personal Voice included, the spoken verse marked as it goes, with a sleep timer and lock-screen controls. On iPhone and iPad, Mi Speaks subscribers can hand a chapter to its Studio voices.
highlight-in-five-colors.0d2ff8: Highlight in five colors, heart the verses you return to, and attach a note to one or more passages — a Sunday sermon on Romans 8:1–17, say. Export your notes as a PDF, Markdown or plain text.
import-a-study-bible.5287cb: Import a study Bible and its notes join the Commentary panel, with its book introductions, essays, maps and pictures kept apart from the text.
iphone-ipad-mac-and.8476c7: iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch, in step through your own iCloud.
licenses-are-being-requested.d031a8: Licenses are being requested from their publishers. If they are granted, each will ship sealed and encrypted, the way the NASB 2020 already does.
make-a-keepsake-of.5d6bbd: Make a keepsake of your highlights and notes for your family: one file, optionally protected with a passphrase, that they open and read as you marked it — a digital “Dad's Bible” to hand down.
mark-what-matters-keep.1e1afc: Mark what matters, keep what you heard on Sunday, and bring years of notes with you.
no-ads-no-analytics.490c17: No ads. No analytics. No third-party SDKs. Your notes travel only through your own iCloud.
nothing-between-you-and.27b4f3: Nothing between you and the text
on-an-ipad-a.d5996f: On an iPad, a Mac or an iPhone on its side, a chapter lays out in two columns and turns page by page with a swipe.
open-a-bible-pdf.bea5ae: Open a Bible PDF with a text layer and Scripture Alone reads it from how it is typeset: headings, verse numbers and footnotes in their places. Locked PDFs are refused.
open-a-passage-get.c382aa: Open a passage, get a verse in any translation, make a verse image or add a note from Shortcuts and Siri. Notes and favorites can appear in Spotlight.
photograph-the-sermon-slide.813c96: Photograph the sermon slide and on-device text recognition starts your note: titled from the slide, linked to every passage on it, its points ready as bullets. The photo is discarded unless you keep it.
put-any-two-side.7c4144: Put any two side by side, verse for verse, and see where they part company — including a translation you read online with your own key.
scripture-alone-speaks-nine.957b69: Scripture Alone speaks nine languages, and each comes with a whole Bible of its own that keeps its own book names and verse numbers.
send-a-verse-to.58d5d6: Send a verse to a friend, or your whole marked-up Bible to your family.
set-the-way-it.444ce2: Set the way it was written
seven-typefaces-adjustable-size.16f95c: Seven typefaces, adjustable size and line spacing, five themes — Auto, Light, Sepia, Dark and Black — and an accent color of your choosing. Read in paragraphs or verse by verse, with full Dynamic Type support.
share-your-notes-and.6116ef: Share your notes and highlights with family as you keep adding to them, not only as a keepsake file.
tap-a-verse-for.021f01: Tap a verse for the Hebrew or Greek behind it, word by word, with parsing, Strong's numbers and a lexicon entry for each. It works in every translation, and downloads once the first time you open it.
the-nasb-2020-the.2f3b2b: The NASB 2020, the NASB 1995 and the American Standard Version ship sealed: signed by a key the app pins, decrypted a chapter at a time, searchable without their text ever lying in the open on your device. It's the format the NASB 2020 and NASB 1995 are licensed in — read how it works.
the-new-american-standard.23f02c: The New American Standard Bible — NASB 2020 is on your device from the moment the app installs, so it reads offline before you ever connect. The NASB 1995, the American Standard Version, the Berean Standard Bible and the King James Version download once, the first time you choose one, and are yours offline from then on. Every one has full-text search.
the-word-and-nothing.59b9cc: The Word, and nothing in the way.
the-words-of-christ.c6c665: The words of Christ in red, section headings, poetry laid out as poetry, and footnotes a tap away.
two-columns-like-a.e60592: Two columns, like a printed Bible
type-jn-3-16.ee05d2: Type “jn 3 16” or “rom 8:28-39” to jump to a passage, or search for any word or phrase. Recent chapters and recent searches are waiting when you come back.
verse-of-the-day.798396: Verse of the Day and Favorites & Notes widgets for the Home and Lock Screens, and an Apple Watch app with the NASB 2020 built in — it follows the translation you're reading on your iPhone, which sends it any other Bible you use — plus your favorites and notes, and a complication with the day's reference.
years-of-notes-in.6859a3: Years of notes in another Bible app don't have to be left behind. Import a Life Bible (formerly Tecarta) export directly, or paste notes or a CSV from anywhere else. Importing twice is safe — anything already there is left alone.
your-highlights-notes-and.4c0001: Your highlights, notes and favorites follow you across iPhone, iPad, Mac and Apple Watch through your own private iCloud. No account, no server — I never see your data.
